argument_summary: The supportable position is narrower than a clean compliance claim. The admissible record supports certification on current aggregate readiness grounds, because the current release clears aggregate launch readiness by 2.5 percentage points and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, while also showing a material developer-support migration subgroup regression 1.1 percentage points below the warning threshold. Under the policy text, prior approval and the informal monitoring note cannot substitute for current-release documentation or reviewed risk acceptance. On this record, the defensible reading is caveated compliance only: certification is supportable if treated as contingent on current-release materials reflecting current results and expressly disclosing the named subgroup weakness, rather than as evidence of already-completed clean compliance.
claims_about_policy: The policy allows certification only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. The admissible evidence supports the aggregate-readiness portion of that standard and identifies the subgroup weakness that must be addressed. The same admissible evidence also shows that prior approval and informal monitoring are contextual only and do not satisfy the documentation or mitigation requirement. So the correct policy characterization is not unconditional compliance, but a constrained, caveated compliance rationale grounded in current results plus required disclosure.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is needed to support this position. The argument rests on the policy standard and the admissible evidence alone.
concessions: No admissible current-release model-card or certification artifact is in evidence showing that the subgroup weakness has already been disclosed in the release materials.
No admissible approved mitigation, exception, or reviewed risk-acceptance record covers the developer-support migration regression.
Prior approval of the same model family and the release-thread monitoring comment cannot independently cure the current documentation gap under the stated policy.
